description: Real open-access articles from Europe PMC, committed verbatim so the offline suite sees the shapes publishers actually emit rather than the shapes a test author already knew about.

articles.title: The evolving landscape of artificial intelligence in patient education: A bibliometric knowledge mapping study
articles.inCorpusBecause: Its publisher-id is a DOI wearing an underscore (10.1177_20552076251406653), which is the shape that provoked the empty-typed-article-id and pattern-recovery defects; it also carries pmcid-ver and the corpus's heaviest table load at eight table-wrap captions, alongside three figure and two supplementary-material captions.

articles.title: Advancing a Hybrid Decision-Making Model in Anesthesiology: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in the Perioperative Setting
articles.inCorpusBecause: A publisher-id that is a bare journal slug, healthcare-14-00097, unlike the DOI-with-underscore and the bare numeric forms elsewhere in the corpus. It is also the only article whose section titles carry ordinal numbering (22 of them, 3.1. through 3.7.), against zero in every other article, which is the shape the recursive section digest flattens into its Parent > Child paths.

articles.title: Evaluating the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Breast Self-Examination
articles.inCorpusBecause: The degenerate end of the range: 29 KB, one table, no figures, no supplementary material, no sub-articles, and a body with no <sec> at all. A corpus of only rich articles cannot tell an empty collection from a dropped one. Its single table also carries the labelled <table-wrap-foot><fn> that #157 is about.

articles.title: pH-dependent 11° F1FO ATP synthase sub-steps reveal insight into the FO torque generating mechanism
articles.inCorpusBecause: Peer-review sub-articles (editor-report, decision-letter, reply) whose prose must stay out of the article body, and figure supplements nested inside their parent <fig> — the shape #156 is about, where the parent figure is dropped. Twelve figure captions, the most in the corpus.

articles.title: Candidate orphan genes: Reassessing uniqueness
articles.inCorpusBecause: Carries no publisher-id element at all, so identifier handling is exercised against absence and not only against three present spellings. Twelve supplementary-material captions, the heaviest load in the corpus of the second commonest caption host in the wild, and all 72 references are <mixed-citation> — the shape #155 is about.

articles.title: Differences in canine serum N-glycosylation pattern during infection and pregnancy
articles.inCorpusBecause: The only <media> captions in the corpus, six of them. Media is the fourth commonest caption host in the wild and one of the hosts the caption-host defect mis-routed, and it was absent from the corpus until this article was added.

articles.title: Extreme heat and cause-specific risk of hospital admission in the adult population in England: a case time series analysis
articles.inCorpusBecause: The only <boxed-text> caption in the corpus, the rarest caption host in the wild at 27 of 2726. It is BMJ Open's STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS OF THIS STUDY block, which that journal puts on essentially every article, and its caption title is exactly what the caption-host defect used to rename the enclosing section to. Also carries a <media> nested inside a <fig>.
